card.name: Neuromuscular blockade and twitch response text
card.fires_on: Words in neuromuscular blockade passages, such as the end of 'neuromuscular', or small words like 'of', 'the' and 'reduced' just before 'muscle twitch response' or 'ED 95'. It appears in anesthesia labels about muscle relaxants and reversal agents.

modes.label: Linking words before twitch recovery
modes.description: Small words such as 'of' and 'the' right before 'the muscle twitch response' after a recovery percentage.
modes.example: The times from 25% recovery<< of>> the muscle twitch response to a T

modes.label: Inside 'neuromuscular blockade'
modes.description: The 'cular' ending of 'neuromuscular' in table titles about muscle relaxant dosing.
modes.example: neuromuscular blockade has not been studied. Table 4 Dosage of Muscle Relaxant Causing 95% Depression in Neuromus<<cular>> Blockade Desflurane Concentration

modes.label: Verbs reducing muscle-relaxant effect
modes.description: Verbs or small words like 'reduced' and 'diminishing' before the effect on relaxants or acetylcholine release.
modes.example: Neuromuscular Blocking Agents Anesthetic concentrations of desflurane at equilibrium (administered for 15 or more minutes before testing)<< reduced>> the ED 95 of succin

card.writes: It seems to push toward muscle-tension and contraction words such as tension, contracted and functional.
card.plain: It fires on text about muscle relaxants and how well muscle twitching recovers after blockade.
